lines.text: When you hit send on ChatGPT, you think it reads your message.
lines.see: Phone, thumb hits send, flash, token sparks already flying (busy frame 0)

lines.text: It can't. It gets chopped into tokens, tiny scraps of words.
lines.see: The message splits into coloured token blocks with a clack each, counter climbs

lines.text: They race to a data centre, into chips that cost as much as a car. Each.
lines.see: Tokens streak down a fibre line to an isometric data centre, dive into a glowing GPU, $30,000+ price tag stamps

lines.text: And it doesn't know the answer. It guesses.
lines.see: Inside the chip: neural lattice lights up, IT DOESN'T KNOW -> IT GUESSES

lines.text: One token at a time, through billions of numbers.
lines.see: Next-token probability bars, the winner pops into the reply bubble, repeats faster and faster

lines.text: One reply uses what a light bulb burns in two minutes.
lines.see: LED bulb fades up, a 2:00 timer runs, 0.34 Wh label

lines.text: Tiny. Until it's two and a half billion messages. Every day.
lines.see: One bulb multiplies into a wall of thousands, counter races into the billions

lines.text: Sam Altman says your please and thank you cost OpenAI tens of millions of dollars.
lines.see: please / thank you tokens drop into a money counter, quote card: tens of millions of dollars well spent

lines.text: So, do you still say please when you hit send?
lines.see: Back to the phone: please typed, thumb hovers send, comment bubble. Last frame matches frame 0 (loop)

facts.claim: Text is split into tokens, chunks of about three quarters of a word
Data-center AI chips cost about $30,000 to $40,000 each (Nvidia Blackwell, Jensen Huang)
An average ChatGPT query uses about 0.34 Wh, what a high-efficiency light bulb uses in a couple of minutes (Sam Altman, The Gentle Singularity)
ChatGPT handles over 2.5 billion prompts a day
Altman: people saying please and thank you costs OpenAI 'tens of millions of dollars well spent'
